title: Gold Retreats From One-Week High as Firmer Dollar, Rate-Hike Bets Take Hold
excerpt: Friday's rally to $4,399 an ounce unwound Monday as profit-taking met a stronger dollar and a synchronized central-bank tightening wave, with the Bank of Japan joining the Fed and ECB.
body:
• Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,349.99 an ounce on Monday, retreating from Friday's one-week high of $4,399.41 as traders took profits and a firmer dollar weighed on the metal.
  • A synchronized round of central-bank tightening — the Bank of Japan joining the Federal Reserve and the ECB — has traders pricing an 88% chance of a December US rate hike, the biggest drag on non-yielding bullion.
  • Continued sliding oil prices unwound the inflation-fear bid that had powered Friday's rally, with hopes for diplomatic progress on Iran ahead of this week's UN meeting.
  • In India, the IBJA benchmark put 24-carat gold at ₹1,53,056 per 10 grams (down ₹671), with retail rates in major cities around ₹1,54,000–1,54,700.

Gold's Friday rally didn't survive the weekend. Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,349.99 an ounce by 1046 GMT on Monday, giving back Friday's run to a one-week high of $4,399.41, while US gold futures slid 0.8% to $4,387.80, according to Reuters. The pullback was a clean reversal of the forces that lifted the metal days earlier: the same "oil slide eases inflation fears" bid that powered Friday's gains unwound, met by profit-taking and a stronger dollar.

"The slightly firmer US dollar is adding to the pressure in gold, while some profit-taking after Friday's rebound is also playing a role," said Ricardo Evangelista, Director and CEO of ActivTrades. The stronger greenback made dollar-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies, capping demand from Asia and Europe.

A tightening wave, now global

The deeper drag came from central banks. On Friday the Bank of Japan became the latest major central bank to tighten, following rate increases by the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank — a synchronized hawkish turn that undercuts gold, which pays no yield. Traders are now pricing an 88% probability of a US rate hike in December, per CME FedWatch.

"Gold remains caught between geopolitical and safe-haven support on one side and restrictive US monetary policy on the other, with the outlook for inflation and the pace of additional Fed hikes likely to remain the key drivers."

— Soojin Kim, MUFG

Oil extended its slide to the lowest in more than a week on Monday as investors hoped for diplomatic progress on the Iran conflict ahead of this week's UN meeting, with prices down 2% on easing concerns over Saudi pipeline flows despite Houthi rebel attacks. The unwind of the oil-inflation bid — the very mechanism behind Friday's gold high — removed the immediate catalyst for further gains.

The Iran floor

Geopolitics remains gold's counterweight, and it is not going away. On Sunday, Iran and the United States exchanged new threats: President Trump warned Tehran would fail economically or face its leadership being "wiped out" unless it struck a deal, while the Iranian military vowed harsh retaliation against any fresh attack, Reuters reported. As long as that standoff simmers, safe-haven demand puts a floor under the metal.

"Persistent inflation and further monetary tightening could create downside towards $4,000. On the other hand, a de-escalation in the US-Iran war could ease inflationary fears, leading to lower yields and a softer dollar, which could allow gold to approach the $5,000 level."

— Ricardo Evangelista, Director and CEO, ActivTrades

India's rates: a brief window

In India, the pullback showed up quickly. The IBJA bullion benchmark put 24-carat gold at ₹1,53,056 per 10 grams, down ₹671 on the day, with 22-carat at ₹1,40,199. Retail rates in major cities tracked around ₹1,54,000–1,54,700 per 10 grams for 24-carat — ₹1,54,250 in Mumbai, ₹1,53,960 in Delhi, ₹1,54,350 in Bengaluru, ₹1,54,670 in Chennai, ₹1,54,470 in Hyderabad and ₹1,54,020 in Kolkata, per Livemint-via-Inshorts. (Methodologies differ across outlets; IBJA's wholesale benchmark runs slightly below retail listings.) Silver fell ₹2,346 to ₹2.35 lakh per kilogram.

For Indian buyers, the retreat offers a brief window after Friday's spike — though with a synchronized global tightening cycle now priced in, any recovery toward $5,000 depends less on festival buying than on whether the US-Iran standoff de-escalates and yields soften. The next US inflation print and the December rate decision are the dates that matter most.
nri_angle: Indian gold buyers get a brief window after Friday's spike, though the global rate-hike cycle now priced in will drive the metal's next move.
